newsitem.title: USA: $1 million bond for Florida synagogue bomb suspect.
newsitem.headline: $1 million bond for Florida synagogue bomb suspect.

text.p: A Florida judge set a $1 million bond on Wednesday for an Orthodox Jew charged with planting a bomb in a Jacksonville synagogue before a speech by former Israeli Prime Minister Shimon Peres.
Harry Shapiro, 31, surrendered to police late on Monday and was charged with placing a destructive device and making a bomb threat. He tried to blame an Arab group, police said.
Shapiro, a former kosher butcher who worked as a cashier at a gas station, planted a pipe bomb at the Jacksonville Jewish Centre "with the intent to disrupt the speech of Shimon Peres," police said.
Duval County Circuit Judge Karen Cole ordered Shapiro held on $1 million bond. He had not posted bail and remained in Jacksonville's pretrial detention centre on Wednesday.

In a police report, investigators said acquaintances had identified Shapiro's voice on a recording of a 911 call made on Feb. 13, the day Peres spoke. The caller said he was with "the American fringe of the Islamic Jihad" and warned that two bombs had been placed at the centre.
The building was evacuated and searched before Peres spoke but the bomb was not found. It was discovered on Saturday, nine days later, by children playing there.
The Jacksonville Sheriff's Office declined comment on Wednesday on why the search failed to turn up the bomb.

"It was one of those situations where the scene there at the location was under the control of the (U.S.) State Department and Shimon Peres' own security people," sheriff's spokesman Harry Reagan said. "We assisted them."
Authorities would not comment on how powerful the bomb was, how close it was to Peres and why it did not go off.

"This was a very serious crime in which a terrible tragedy was narrowly averted," said Art Teitelbaum, southern area director of the Anti-Defamation League, which tracks hate crimes and attacks on Jewish institutions.

Peres became prime minister after a right-wing Jew named Yigal Amir assassinated Yitzhak Rabin in November 1995. Amir was infuriated by their accord with the Palestinians, which involved handing back occupied lands for peace.
Peres lost the subsequent election to hardliner Benjamin Netanyahu after a string of Arab bombings soured many Israelis on the peace process.

Alan Margolies, director of the Jacksonville Jewish Federation, said Peres visited the city to deliver a speech on his vision for Middle East peace and to raise money for the Peres Institute for Peace. He said he could not comment on the bomb incident while the investigation was ongoing.

Shapiro operated a Jacksonville butcher shop called Kosher Kuts from 1991 to 1993 and moved to New York after closing it. Acquaintances described him as an observant Jew who attended a conservative synagogue as a child and often wore a yarmulke.

Michael Bossen, a Jacksonville attorney who knew the suspect, told the Florida Times-Union that Shapiro was "a very extreme, very intense individual. He'd get caught up in little things. He'd had a very, very bad temper."
